requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must contain at least 12 actual characters.
requirements.summary: The persistent policy sets minlen=12 and disables character-class length credits. An 11-character, four-class password was rejected while a 12-character, four-class password was accepted, including after restart; PAM references pam_pwquality.

requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must use at least three character classes.
requirements.summary: The persistent policy sets minclass=3. A 12-character password using two classes was rejected, while a four-class password was accepted, including after restart.

overall_summary: Both requested password-policy outcomes are satisfied with persistent configuration and direct boundary tests. The mandatory node-restart protocol is coherently demonstrated and independently corroborated. Hygiene is strong, with only minor possible retained backup/log artifacts.
limitations: Enforcement was tested through pwscore and corroborated by PAM configuration rather than through an end-to-end non-root passwd transaction.
Native package-health checks timed out both before and after execution, so package consistency could not be independently assessed.
Lifecycle temporary-file inventory covers /tmp but not /etc or /var/tmp, so retention of the policy backup and reboot log is inferred from their creation and the absence of cleanup evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: The intended pwquality configuration was the only substantive system change, and post-executor observations show no failed services or unexpected listening sockets. The restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart policy state, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle observations, active sshd, persisted configuration, and successful post-restart enforcement tests. Two minor residual artifacts lack cleanup evidence: the rollback backup /etc/security/pwquality.conf.antrieb-pre-policy created by cmd-47d40b41577641bd and /var/tmp/antrieb-reboot.log created by cmd-b270b90477744e08 appear retained, though the former had a legitimate safety role. Temporary verification files from the failed post-restart attempt were subsequently removed by cmd-0ac6a8dfd2694216. No other unnecessary mutation is evident.
